 Judgment

1. All these four appeals arise out of the common judgment and award dated 03.02.2020 passed in MVC Nos.183/2017 and 138/2017 by II Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Vijayapura (hereinafter referred to as 'Tribunal' for short).

sentences.text: 2. Claimants-petitioners in both MVC Nos.183/2017 and 138/2017 as well as respondent-Insurer in both the cases aggrieved by the judgment and award passed by the learned II Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT VIII, Vijayapura dated 02.03.2020 have filed these appeals.

sentences.text: 3. All these four appeals have come up for hearing on 'Admission' and with the consent of learned Counsels for the parties they are taken up for 'Final disposal'.
4. For the sake of convenience, we refer the parties as per their rank before the Tribunal.

5. It was the case of the claimants in both the cases that on 15.12.2016 at about 3.30 p.m., deceased Ram Harijan @ Mayakeri along with his friend Dattatreya @ Datta Mane were going towards Nad B.K. in Car bearing registration No.KA-33/M-2532 on Vijaypura to Solapur Road.
They met with accident at Dhulakhed due to rash and negligent driving of the bus bearing registration KA- 28/F-1690 by its driver.
Due to impact, the driver of the car as well as Ram Harijan and Datta Mane had sustained grievous injuries.
The driver of the car as well as Ram Harijan died at the spot and Datta Mane has died on 16.12.2016 while undergoing treatment at hospital.
Claimants in MVC No.183/2017 are widow, minor children and parents of deceased Ram Harijan and claimants in MVC No.138/2017 are widow and minor children of deceased Datta Mane.
7. Both the claimants in respective petitions had claimed compensation for the death of Ram Harijan as well as Datta Mane.
8. The respondent - Corporation has contended that accident was taken place due to rash and negligent driving of Car by its driver.
It has denied all other averments stated in the petition.
It has also contended that amount of compensation claimed by the claimants are exorbitant.
With these reasons, respondent - Corporation prayed to dismiss the petitions.
9. The Tribunal has clubbed both claim petitions and recorded the common evidence.

Claimants have examined PWs.1 to 3 and got marked documents as per Exs.P1 to P11.
- 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1550-DB 10.

The Tribunal on hearing of both sides and appreciating pleadings and evidence partly allowed the petitions by awarding compensation of Rs.7,75,000/- in MVC.No.183/2017 and Rs.8,20,000/-
in MVC No.138/2017 and held that the respondent-Corporation is liable to pay the compensation.
11. We have heard the arguments of learned Advocates for the parties and perused the material available on record.
12. The learned counsel for the claimants have vehemently contended that the Tribunal has not considered the income of the deceased properly.
The deceased were agriculturist and earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
The Tribunal has not considered the said income and has taken the notional income of the deceased at Rs.5,000/- per month in each case, which is on much lower side.

which is usually taken while settlement of the dispute before the Lok Adalat - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1550-DB for the accident of the year 2015 and the same could be applied in the present case.
He has further stated that Tribunal has not considered future prospects of the deceased, which needs to be added to the income of the deceased in both the petitions.
The learned counsel for the claimants has also submitted that the amount of compensation awarded under other heads are meager.
Therefore, prayed to enhance the amount of compensation.
13. The learned counsel for respondent - Corporation contended that the Tribunal has not at all considered the rash and negligent driving of the car by its driver.
Looking to the charge sheet itself

,
it clearly indicates that the accident has taken place due to negligence of driver of car.
He has further submitted that amount of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on higher side without any basis.
Therefore, prays to dismiss the appeals filed by the claimants.

14. Following points emerge for our determination:
- 12 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1550-DB i.
Whether the Tribunal is justified in holding that accident has taken due to rash and negligent driving of bus by its driver?
ii. Whether the claimants are entitled for enhancement of the compensation awarded by the Tribunal?
15. The evidence of PWs.1 to 3 reveals that accident was taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the bus by its driver.
To rebut the said evidence the driver of the bus was not examined by the respondent.
The Investigating Officer after thorough investigation filed charge sheet against the driver of the bus and it was not challenged by the respondent.
These facts clearly indicate that accident was taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the bus by its driver.

The Tribunal by appreciating the pleadings and evidence in this regard, has rightly held that accident has taken place due to negligence on the part of driver of the bus and it does not call for any interference by this Court.
- 13 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1550-DB 16. QUANTUM OF COMPENSATION IN MFA NO.200631/2020 a) The MFA No. 200631/2020

arises out of MVC No.183/2017, in which the Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased as Rs.5,000/- per month, deducted 1/4 of income towards his personal Managing Director Nekrtc Gulbarga vs Chandrabhaga W/O Ram Harijan @ Mayakeri ... on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183152443/
8 expenses and applied multiplier as '15' and awarded the compensation of Rs.6,75,000/- towards 'loss of dependency'.

The Tribunal has also assessed the evidence and awarded following amount of compensation under different heads:

 b) It is not in dispute that the age of the deceased at the time of accident was 38 years.
The dispute is in respect - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1550-DB of income of the deceased.
According to the claim petition, deceased was an agriculturist and earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
It is true that the claimants are unable to substantiate their case to prove the income of the deceased.
Therefore, the Tribunal has taken notional income of the deceased as Rs.5,000/- by per month.
The accident has taken place during the year 2016.

As rightly submitted by learned counsel for appellants - claimants, while settlement of disputes in Lok Adalat, for the accident taken place in the year 2016, notional income of the victim is taken as Rs.8,750/- per month.
The same could be applied to the facts of the present case and the income of the deceased is taken as Rs.8,750/-.
c) The Tribunal has not considered future prospects of the deceased.
Deceased died at the age of 38 years.

Therefore, as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others1 the future prospects to an extent of 40% has to 2017 ACJ 2700 - 15 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1550-DB be added to the earnings of the deceased.

In this case also the claimants have contended that the deceased was earning Rs.15,000/-
per annum from agriculture and they were unable to prove it.

Therefore, the Tribunal has taken the income of the deceased as Rs.5,000/- per month and has also assessed the evidence and awarded following amount of compensation under different heads:
1 Loss of income due to Rs.7,20,000/-
dependency 2 Loss of love and affection Rs.25,000/- 3 Loss of Estate Rs.20,000/-
4 Loss of consortium Rs.30,000/-
5 Transportation and funeral Rs.25,000/-
 expenses  TOTAL Rs.8,20,000/-
 - 18 -  NC: 2023:KHC-K:1550-DB  b) As discussed above, Rs.8,750/- shall be taken as notional income of the deceased since he died in the accident of the year 2016 and 40% of the said income has to be added towards future prospects and  of the said income has to be deducted towards his personal expenses.
Therefore, the income of the deceased on which the claimants were dependent was Rs.9,188/-.
It is not in dispute that the appropriate multiplier applicable is '16'.
Therefore, the compensation for which claimants are entitled under the head 'loss of dependency' is Rs.9,188/- x 12 x 16 = 17,64,096/-.

c) As discussed in the above Paragraphs and as per law laid down in the cases of PRANAY SETHI and Magma General Insurance Company Limited (referred supra) each of the claimants are entitled for a sum of Rs.40,000/- towards 'loss of consortium' and 'love and affection'.
As there are four dependants a sum of Rs.1,60,000/- shall be awarded under the said head.
Towards 'funeral expenses' and 'loss of estate, a sum of Rs.15,000/- each is awarded.

opennyai_summary.facts:
They met with accident at Dhulakhed due to rash and negligent driving of the bus bearing registration KA- 28/F-1690 by its driver.
Due to impact, the driver of the car as well as Ram Harijan and Datta Mane had sustained grievous injuries.
The driver of the car as well as Ram Harijan died at the spot and Datta Mane has died on 16.12.2016 while undergoing treatment at hospital.
7. Both the claimants in respective petitions had claimed compensation for the death of Ram Harijan as well as Datta Mane.
8. The respondent - Corporation has contended that accident was taken place due to rash and negligent driving of Car by its driver.
9. The Tribunal has clubbed both claim petitions and recorded the common evidence.
The Tribunal on hearing of both sides and appreciating pleadings and evidence partly allowed the petitions by awarding compensation of Rs.7,75,000/- in MVC.No.183/2017 and Rs.8,20,000/-
in MVC No.138/2017 and held that the respondent-Corporation is liable to pay the compensation.
opennyai_summary.arguments: The deceased were agriculturist and earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
opennyai_summary.issue:
14. Following points emerge for our determination:
- 12 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1550-DB i.
Whether the Tribunal is justified in holding that accident has taken due to rash and negligent driving of bus by its driver?
ii. Whether the claimants are entitled for enhancement of the compensation awarded by the Tribunal?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
These facts clearly indicate that accident was taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the bus by its driver.
According to the claim petition, deceased was an agriculturist and earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
Therefore, the Tribunal has taken notional income of the deceased as Rs.5,000/- by per month.
The accident has taken place during the year 2016.
As rightly submitted by learned counsel for appellants - claimants, while settlement of disputes in Lok Adalat, for the accident taken place in the year 2016, notional income of the victim is taken as Rs.8,750/- per month.
The same could be applied to the facts of the present case and the income of the deceased is taken as Rs.8,750/-.
c) The Tribunal has not considered future prospects of the deceased.
Deceased died at the age of 38 years.
It is not in dispute that the appropriate multiplier applicable is '16'.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Multiplier applicable to case in hand is '15'.

9  deceased  Add 40% future  prospects Rs.3,500/-
 Rs.12,250/-
 Less 1/4th personal  expenses Rs.3,062/-
 Net Income Rs.9,188/-
On the basis of the said calculations, the claimants are entitled for compensation to be awarded under the head 'loss of dependency' is Rs.9,188 x 12 x 15 (multiplier) = 16,53,840/-.
d)
In this case in all there are six claimants, therefore, a sum of Rs.2,40,000/- is awarded towards 'loss of consortium' and 'love and affection'.
e) Claimants are also entitled for compensation of Rs.15,000/- each under the conventional head of 'loss of estate' and 'funeral expenses'.
f) From the above said discussions, following amount of compensation is awarded to the claimants in MVC.No.183/2017:
Amount in  No. Rs.
 1. Loss of dependency 16,53,840/-
 2. Loss of consortium and love 2,40,000/-
 and affection
3 . Loss of estate 15,000/-
 4. Towards funeral expenses 15,000/-
 Total 19,23,840/-
Claimants are entitled to enhancement of Rs.11,48,840/-.
Therefore, the income of the deceased on which the claimants were dependent was Rs.9,188/-.
Therefore, the compensation for which claimants are entitled under the head 'loss of dependency' is Rs.9,188/- x 12 x 16 = 17,64,096/-.
c) As discussed in the above Paragraphs and as per law laid down in the cases of PRANAY SETHI and Magma General Insurance Company Limited (referred supra) each of the claimants are entitled for a sum of Rs.40,000/- towards 'loss of consortium' and 'love and affection'.
As there are four dependants a sum of Rs.1,60,000/- shall be awarded under the said head.
Towards 'funeral expenses' and 'loss of estate, a sum of Rs.15,000/- each is awarded.
From the above said discussions, following amount of compensation is awarded for the claimants in MVC No.138/2017:
 Sl.No.
Amount in  Rs.
1. Loss of dependency 17,64,096  2. Loss of consortium and love 1,60,000  and affection
3 . Loss of estate 15,000
4. Funeral expenses 15,000  Total 19,54,096
Claimants are entitled for enhancement of Rs.11,34,096/-.
18.
For the above said discussions, we answer point Nos.1 and 2 accordingly and pass the following:
- 20 -  NC: 2023:KHC-K:1550-DB  ORDER i.
The MFA Nos.200631/2020 and 200629/2020 are partly allowed with costs.
ii. The MFA Nos.200233/2021 and MFA.No.200256/2021 are dismissed.
Director
Claimants in MVC No. 183/2017 are entitled for compensation of Rs.19,23,840/-
as against 17,75,000/- awarded by the Tribunal and they are entitled for enhancement of Rs.11,48,840/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. on enhanced amount from the date of petition till its payment.
b. Claimants in MVC No. 138/2017 are entitled for compensation of Rs.19,54,096/-
- 21 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:1550-DB as against 8,20,000/- awarded by the Tribunal and they are entitled for enhancement of Rs.11,34,096/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till its payment.
c. Respondent - Corporation shall pay the enhanced amount of compensation with interest within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order in both the case.
d. The findings of the Tribunal regarding apportionment, deposit and release of the amount are kept intact.
e. Office shall transmit the deposit of amount by Corporation to Tribunal for disbursement to claimants.
